summary.text: Gregory W. Meeks is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 5th Congressional District. A lawyer and former Queens prosecutor, he served in the New York State Assembly from 1993 to 1998 before winning a 1998 special election to Congress; he represented NY-6 until 2013 and NY-5 since. He is the Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, which he chaired in the 117th Congress, and also sits on the Financial Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in East Harlem, New York City (1953, per Wikipedia). According to his official biography, his family came north from Rock Hill, South Carolina, during the Great Migration, and he grew up in a public housing project.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Adelphi University (1975) and a law degree from Howard University (1978).

Served as an assistant district attorney of Queens County (1978–1983), then as assistant special narcotics prosecutor of New York City, deputy counsel of a New York state investigation commission, and supervising judge of the New York workers' compensation board.
Elected to the New York State Assembly in 1992, representing the 31st District, and served until 1998.
Won a 1998 special election to the U.S. House and represented New York's 6th District until 2013, then the redrawn 5th District from 2013.

On the Financial Services Committee, served as chair of its Subcommittee on Consumer Protection and Financial Institutions; his official biography says he was a Dodd-Frank conferee and co-authored several provisions of that law.
Became the first Black member of Congress to chair the House Foreign Affairs Committee in the 117th Congress (2021–2023) and is its Ranking Member.
According to his official biography, he is a member of the New Democrat Coalition and co-chairs its Trade Task Force; Wikipedia also lists him as chair of the Queens County Democratic Party.
